2197.unvetted: Edition match needed before a verdict. Manus 750696 (JSON read 6 Nov 2026) confirms 'Presente testo cifrato alle pp. 172-173; p. 180' in APUG Concilio di Trento 242rec, 34 Contarini->Farnese letters 30 Mar-4 Jul 1541 'cop. dagli originali', with Pallavicino's marginalia; no images. But the despatches are printed: Pastor, 'Die Correspondenz des Cardinals Contarini waehrend seiner deutschen Legation (1541)', Historisches Jahrbuch 1 (1880) 321 ff. and 473 ff. (archive.org historischesjahr01gruoft, read), prints from Bibl. Pia 129 ff. 172-323 (copy 'tratta dal registro del Card. Contarini') the Regensburg letters to Farnese of April-July 1541 in clear, e.g. no. 99 of 19 June (pp. 483-486), which Dittrich, Regesten und Briefe des Cardinals Gasparo Contarini (1881; archive.org bub_gb_PrnQAAAAMAAJ, read) calls 'zum Theil chiffrirt' in all copies (Cod. 129, Cod. Trid. 98); Pastor also restores passages that Schulze (ZKG 3, 1879) lacked because the Naples copies left the cipher unsolved. So the plaintext of the APUG cipher passages is very probably in print, but pp. 172-180 cannot be assigned to a letter without the APUG pages (the volume ends 4 Jul; Pastor notes that Pallavicino cited a 4 Jul letter missing from the Vatican copies, which may be the one at p. 180). known.py (APUG, Contarini, Gregoriana, Ratisbona): no other copy of this volume; not on DECODE. Needs APUG pp. 170-181 to compare with Pastor nos. 99-108 and Dittrich.

2198.unvetted: No ciphertext shown and the edition not opened. Manus 724628 (JSON read 6 Nov 2026): title 'Lettere in cifra intorno al C. di T. dal 1546 al 1547 (c. 1)'; 'Registro di lettere di Giambattista Cervini al card. Cervini; scritte da Roma a Trento 11. IV. 1546 - 30. VIII. 1547; cop. sec. XVII dalle Carte cerviniane. Al f. 83r vi e un elenco delle cifre usate'. A 17th-century register copied from the Cervini papers under that title is as likely to hold the deciphered texts of letters sent in cipher as the groups themselves; nothing in the record says groups are on the leaves, and Manus links no images (APUG, Rome). Concilium Tridentinum X (Epistularum pars prima, ed. Buschbell, 1916) covers the 1545-47 legation correspondence and is said to print the Cervini letters in part; the archive.org copy (conciliumtrident0010coun) is lending-only (djvu text 403 on 6 Nov 2026), so not opened. Web searches on Giambattista Cervini cipher letters and on Buschbell/Carte Cerviniane found nothing on this register. known.py (APUG 690, Cervini, cerviniane): only this lead. Needs APUG cc. 1-5 and 83r, and CT X opened at the G.B. Cervini letters.

2199.unvetted: No ciphertext shown. Manus 685212 (JSON read 6 Nov 2026) gives only titles copied from the volume's index ('Tutti i titoli sono stati riportati dall'indice ... senza che sia stata verificata la corrispondenza con i titoli interni'): c. 242 'Littera del Cardinal Borromeo ... al Vescovo di Ventimiglia in Concilio del primo di Luglio 1562. Littera del medesimo al medesimo di 4 Luglio con un'altra in Cifra', and cc. 243-253 'Altre litterae del medesimo al medesimo con li cifre a parte de li 18 di Luglio sino a li v settembre 1562'. So the correspondents are Carlo Borromeo -> Carlo Visconti, bishop of Ventimiglia, at Trent; 'con li cifre a parte' in a copy volume most often means the decrypts were copied after the clear letters. No images (APUG). Prior art also open: Visconti's side is printed (Lettere ... da Carlo Visconti; Aymon, Lettres anecdotes du nonce Visconti, 1719) and Susta, Die roemische Curie und das Concil von Trient unter Pius IV, vols 2-3 (1909-11), covers summer 1562; only Susta vol. 1 (1904, to early 1562) is on archive.org (diermischecurie00usgoog), so the volumes for July-Sept 1562 were not opened. known.py (APUG 588, Ventimiglia, Visconti, Borromeo): no copy of these letters. Needs APUG cc. 240-254 and Susta vols 2-3.

2200.unvetted: No ciphertext shown. Manus 699266 (JSON read 6 Nov 2026), Osservazioni only: 'Cifre di lettere del Concilio di Trento; Cifra sopra il luogo del conte di Luna (ff. 31r-43r)' in a Trent miscellany (Pius IV, Borromeo, Delfino, Visconti). In curial copy volumes 'Cifra' as a heading is the usual label for the deciphered text of a cipher letter; nothing says groups are on ff. 31r-43r, and Manus links no images (APUG). Related item: catalogue 1343 (Ambrosiana Q 123 sup., 'Lettera cifrata sopra il dare il luoco al Conte di Luna', 1563) is very probably another copy of the same letter on the Count of Luna's precedence (June 1563); it too was promoted from titles only, so neither text has been seen. Web searches on the Count of Luna precedence 1563 + cifra/Borromeo found Sarpi's narrative and the Penn Ms. Codex 678 and St John's O.3 legate letter-books, no decipherment of this item; Susta vol. 4 (1914), which prints the legates' 1563 letters, is not on archive.org and was not opened. known.py (APUG 608, conte di Luna, Delfino): only catalogue 1343 as a probable parallel copy. Needs APUG ff. 28-44 and Susta vol. 4.

'Copies of letters sent in cipher' is the wording for decrypts or clear copies as often as for groups. Vat. lat. 14673 is not digitised: the DigiVatLib IIIF manifest returns 404 and its detail page says 'No record match' (6 Nov 2026), while the neighbour Vat. lat. 14672 is online, so the earlier note that the site resets this network no longer applies. Web searches on 'Vat. lat. 14673' Ubaldini and on Ubaldini 1606 cipher/Borghese found only his 1607-16 nunciature letter-books (BL Add MS 8721-8727), nothing on these copies. known.py ('Vat. lat. 14673', 'Ubaldini'): only this lead. Lead access should be 'archive'. Needs the Vatican Library reading room or a scan order for cc. 122r-129v.

2203.unvetted: Cannot be identified well enough to search prior art. Manus 588084 (JSON read 6 Nov 2026), element cc. 147r-197r of BNC Rome Ges. 204: 'Carteggio del Duca di Mantova con un suo invitato a Parigi in parte in cifra, con qualche altra lettera allo stesso duca' (title supplied from the Catalogo dei manoscritti Gesuitici p. 119), first incipit 'Ho poi fatta la mia corsa' (147r), last 'Siccome ho umilmente trasmesso a V. A. S.' (189r-197r), signed and dated letters; neither the Duke, the envoy nor any year is given (other items in the volume run 1656-1775). Cipher is reported by the old catalogue, but its form, and whether decrypts stand with it, are unknown. Ms.Ges.204 is not in the BNCR digital library (searchSignature 'Ms.Ges.204' returned 0; 18 Gesuitico manuscripts are online, 6 Nov 2026). A web search for a Mantua-Paris envoy cipher correspondence in BNCR Gesuitico found nothing. known.py ('Gesuitico 204', 'Duca di Mantova', 'Valenti Gonzaga'): no other copy. Needs BNC Rome cc. 147r-197r (or a scan order) to date the letters, name the envoy and see the cipher before editions (ASMn Gonzaga, Paris envoy series) can be checked.
